country_heterogeneity.note: This is heterogeneity ACROSS PAIRWISE CONTRASTS against one reference, not an omnibus test of country heterogeneity. The frozen capability supports no omnibus test, and none is reported.

cross_country_dif.multiplicity_note: 20 contrasts share one reference and are not independent. No family-wise correction is applied because the frozen decision rule is a prespecified effect-size and information-mass rule, not a p-value; the count of flagged items is reported as a prevalence, never as a significance test.
cross_country_dif.scope: PRESPECIFIED TWO-GROUP REFERENCE-COUNTRY CONTRASTS. The frozen DIF capability (SELECTED_MODEL_5A) reduces settings to (setting > 0), so it supports exactly two groups. A 21-country omnibus contrast is OUTSIDE its validated region and was not run or approximated. Each result below is one country against the reference, and means nothing about any other pair.

known_hazard.P_DPQ.xpt: the NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic file OVERLAPS DPQ_J: its respondents include the 2017-2018 cycle. Using both would double-count those people. P_DPQ is therefore NOT part of this cycle and is not opened.

mapping.rationale: DPQ_J carries the identical DPQ variable block - SEQN, DPQ010-DPQ090, the same 0-3 categories and the same 7/9 administrative codes - so the DPQ_I mapping applies unchanged. Reusing it is what makes the comparison a replication rather than two separate analyses; only dataset_id differs.

metrics.labelling: every comparator quantity is AGREEMENT with a conventional estimate, never accuracy against truth
point_estimate_transfer: cronbach alpha of the item set

prohibited_after_opening: changing the mapping, any protocol parameter, the comparator set or any metric
retraining, fine-tuning, recalibrating or re-thresholding the model
replication_questions: does strong point-estimate transfer replicate in a later population sample?
does the uncertainty mismatch (L45: conservative intervals, ratio ~2) replicate?
does the L44 instrument-not-model conclusion replicate?

binary_group_dif.evidence: 20 two-group reference-country contrasts on ESS7 returned zero flagged items with max |effect| 0.063-0.132 logits against a 0.20 substantive floor, stable under both size-matching and half-sample subsampling
binary_group_dif.why_experimental: a uniform null is consistent with genuine invariance AND with an insensitive head, and the ESS7 design contains no contrast with known DIF that could distinguish them. Absence of a positive control is why this is experimental rather than supported, and a SYNTHETIC positive control does not discharge it - it would establish sensitivity on the data the head was trained against, not on real data

multicountry_dif.reason: INEXPRESSIBLE, not merely unvalidated. dif.group_code_from_settings reduces every setting to (setting > 0), so a k-group design collapses to one group against the other k-1 pooled. A many-country request returns a confident number for a contrast nobody asked for
multicountry_dif.required_decomposition: prespecified two-group contrasts with an explicitly declared reference and focal group, each labelled with that scope

real_world_cross_sectional_point_estimat.measured: agreement with conventional estimators 0.92-0.94 on the two NHANES cycles and 0.97-0.998 on ESS7, no schema revision on any dataset, and 0.95-0.99 against MML-GRM in every one of the 21 ESS countries taken separately
real_world_cross_sectional_point_estimat.scope: cross-sectional only, two instrument families, one construct family (depressive symptomatology), 23 country-cycles. Agreement with conventional estimates is NOT accuracy against truth: the model and its comparators share graded-response assumptions and can be wrong together. No criterion measure has been used

real_world_interval_scale.evidence: calibration ratio (predicted width / empirical variation) median 2.19 on DPQ_I, 2.18 on DPQ_J, and 3.12-10.54 across the ESS7 masking curve - above 1 at every level of every dataset, i.e. consistently conservative. The shape failure is dataset-dependent: monotonicity 0.10 and 0.08 on the NHANES cycles against 0.98 on ESS7 under an identical measurement (L47)

why_the_prohibitions_follow.confidence_interval: a frequentist coverage guarantee was never established
why_the_prohibitions_follow.coverage_interval: nominal coverage is unvalidated; the scale error alone would break it
why_the_prohibitions_follow.literal error_bar: the width runs 2x to 10x the estimate's actual variation, so the bar drawn would not be the error
why_the_prohibitions_follow.probability statement: no probability derived from this width is warranted - the scale it would be read off IS the miscalibrated quantity
why_the_prohibitions_follow.threshold-based individual decision: misplaces every participant relative to a fixed cutoff, and on the NHANES datasets not even consistently between participants. The prohibition with direct consequences for people

real_world_relative_uncertainty.evidence: the uncertainty-error relationship is strongly positive WITHIN participants: median r 0.907 (DPQ_I), 0.88 (DPQ_J) and 0.861 (ESS7), positive for 100%, 100% and 98.7% of participants. Across ESS countries the model's own median relative uncertainty predicts where it agrees least with MML-GRM at r = -0.803, which is this capability doing useful work rather than merely being self-consistent

protocol.balancing: items ordered by endorsement rate; assignment randomised within adjacent pairs
protocol.correction: none; correlations are uncorrected and compare methods, not absolute reliability
protocol.interpretation: if every method falls similarly the loss belongs to the INSTRUMENT; if the model falls substantially further it is a MODEL-TRANSFER issue
never: report a bare split-half number without comparators on the same splits
use an unbalanced or ordered split
infer a model defect from a single split
reported: per-method median, mean, sd, q10, q90 of the split-half correlation
paired difference (model minus comparator) with a 95% interval
fraction of splits on which the model is lower

components.calibration_ratio: predicted / empirical. 1.0 is calibrated; below 1 is overconfident. This is the single number the protocol exists to produce
components.comparator_diagnostics: the same quantities for MML graded response using its EAP posterior standard deviation, where R/mirt is available
components.dataset_level_uncertainty_error: across mask levels: does mean predicted width track RMSE?
components.empirical_variation: the spread of masked estimates around the full-item estimate, across repetitions at the same mask level - what the uncertainty actually is
components.held_out_proper_score: log loss and Brier score on the masked items, scored from the model's own category probabilities - not a correlation, so it cannot be flattered by scale
components.item_prediction_degradation: correlation between the estimate and the held-out responses, by mask level
components.participant_level_uncertainty_error: within participant, across mask levels: does a wider predicted interval accompany a larger actual error?
components.predicted_posterior_width: the model's own interval width per participant at each mask level

protocol.nesting: within a repetition each level removes a superset of the previous level's items
never: summarise uncertainty behaviour with a single masking contrast

read predicted width as an error bar, under any circumstances, whether or not the calibration ratio is known - knowing the ratio is what established that the width is not an error bar, not a licence to treat it as one
recalibrate the frozen model in response to what this protocol finds
reported_per_dataset: the full curve for every component, never endpoints
participant-level monotonicity rate alongside pooled medians
local non-monotonicity with location and magnitude
cross-sectional, trait and state uncertainty separately where applicable

revision.superseded_sha256: the v1.0 hash is recorded in configs/model/phase6b1_protocols.v1.json and in the provenance block of every run made under it; those runs remain valid under v1.0
revision.what_changed: one 'never' clause only. No parameter, seed, mask fraction, component or reported quantity was touched, so no run's numbers change and no result is reinterpreted.
revision.why: v1.0 said 'never read predicted width as an error bar BEFORE the calibration ratio is known'. That conditional was correct when written - the ratio was unknown. It is now known, published in the same artifacts that carry this clause, and above 1 on every dataset. A reader reaching the clause today satisfies its condition and finds it grants exactly the permission the contract forbids. The prohibition is unconditional and is now written that way.

l43_shape.finding: non-monotone participant-level uncertainty under progressive masking

l45_scale.finding: predicted width against empirical variation of the estimate
l45_scale.note: Empirical variation is measured against the full-item estimate, not truth, so it understates true error and the ratio is an upper bound.

uncertainty_error_relationship.definition: Within each participant, across mask levels: that person's own predicted width against that person's own absolute displacement from their own full-information estimate. A positive value licenses RANKING - wider means less certain - and says nothing about the width's scale.

relative_uncertainty.contract: relative ranking and diagnostics only; not a confidence interval, coverage interval, error bar, probability statement, or threshold input

required_citation: European Social Survey European Research Infrastructure (ESS ERIC). ESS Round 7 (2014) Integrated File, edition 2.3 [Data set]. Sikt - Norwegian Agency for Shared Services in Education and Research, Norway. doi:10.21338/NSD-ESS7-2014.

stability.interval_note: The 95% interval is an ordinary sampling interval for a paired difference in split-half correlations across splits. It is NOT a model posterior width and the real-world uncertainty contract does not govern it.
